# harness-quarters

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
*Harness homes, declared links, settings, and session-state hygiene*

Links each agent harness's home to its instructions, skills, settings and hooks, for the
person running agents across these hosts. It keeps model picks and trust out of git,
records what each harness has been shown to do, pins pi and relay, and archives sessions.
The instruction corpus and profiles live in lore; the flow system lives in flows.

Authority: `docs/architecture.md`
<!-- ops:identity end -->

This is a personal reference configuration for coding agents. It depends on
registered sibling projects and private local settings; a clone does not recreate
another person’s working environment. See [architecture](docs/architecture.md) for
responsibilities and owner boundaries.

## Install

Run once per checkout and again after pulling a setup-recipe change:

```sh
just setup
```

Setup installs repository hooks and the required harness-state Git filter, and
creates local configuration directories. It does not generate the private work
Codex config, authenticate a harness or install model runtimes. That file comes
from an already configured host and remains untracked under `local/`.

Home links require registered owner checkouts and existing targets. From main:

```sh
just link
just link-check
```

Inspect the preview before an authorized `just link --apply`. Apply refuses
worktrees and foreign entries. Create the real harness homes before first use;
[home links](docs/home-links.md) explains ownership, first-run adoption and refusal
recovery. Never point a live launcher or home at a temporary worktree.

Pinned runtime installation is separate from setup. Pi and relay upgrades require
reviewed pins, stable installation on each participating host and any needed live
authority; see [runtime operations](docs/architecture.md#pinned-runtimes-and-local-extensions),
[capability probes](docs/harness-capabilities.md#re-probing-pi) and the
[relay runbook](docs/runbooks/relay-runtime.md).

## Usage

Find a previous session from native harness metadata:

```sh
tools/hq sessions -n 20
tools/hq sessions --harness codex --home personal --here
tools/hq sessions -i
```

The interactive selector resumes in the recorded home and working directory after
checking their availability. Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity stores have
different coverage limits; see [sessions](docs/sessions.md).

Read an observed capability without treating a missing observation as false:

```sh
tools/harness-facts list --pretty
tools/harness-facts get controller-wake codex
tools/harness-facts check
```

The standalone `tools/harness-evidence` interface discovers and decodes transcript
evidence, including the opt-in native index profile. Its formats and replay
contract are documented in [sessions](docs/sessions.md#standalone-transcript-decoder);
[capabilities](docs/harness-capabilities.md) distinguishes synthetic conformance
from observed emission.

Session capture, pruning and optional replica operations use `tools/session-archive`.
They need the configured archive/backup destinations and the stated readiness
evidence. [Session archive](docs/session-archive.md) covers its protocol and failure
boundaries; setup alone does not enable user timers.

## Configuration

| Source | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| `links.toml` | Real harness homes, declared links and registered owners |
| `harnesses.toml` | Harness slugs, live config paths, stripped keys and pick units |
| `.gitattributes` | Exact required clean-filter routes |
| `harnesses/` | Tracked settings, hooks and runtime definitions |
| `local/` | Untracked private work Codex config, saved picks and trust |
| `facts/capabilities.toml` | Validated observations with explicit unknown states |
| `tools/hq.toml` | Session selection and launch flags per home |

Model picks, effort and Codex trust are live state. The required clean filter keeps
them out of commits; hooks preserve them across Git transitions. Run setup before
staging harness configuration, and follow [live-state recovery](docs/live-state.md)
if validation refuses. Never disable the required filter or overwrite a live
configuration just to clear a modified marker.

Turn budgets, lifecycle state and paused-task handling are in
[turn pause](docs/turn-pause.md). Home-link application, live hook trust, services,
desktop use and paid capability probes retain their own authorization boundaries.

## Layout

- `harnesses/{claude,codex,agy,pi}/`: settings, hooks, launchers and probes.
- `external/ponytail/`: integration defaults; automatic activation stays off.
- `.githooks/`: live-state filtering, pick/trust preservation and commit gates.
- `tools/harness_stores/`: native session adapters shared by session consumers.
- `tools/harness_evidence/`: standalone native transcript evidence.
- `tools/session_archive/`: capture, prune, replica and restore implementation.
- `tools/turn_pause/`: turn accounting and lifecycle/tool guards.
- `agents/`: session-log guidance, episode extraction and wake judging.
- `relay/`: pinned standalone runtime and subscriber configuration.
- `systemd/user/`: optional archive units.
- `docs/`: current references and runbooks.

Developer entry points are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Run focused checks through
`just test-one <pytest arguments>` and mandatory `just check-hygiene` before
committing. Automatic broad tests are disabled by the declared policy; a skip is
not a pass. `TT_FORCE=1 just test` deliberately requests the full suite.

Historical working documents and exact private probe evidence live in private
records. Normal manifest/fact/fixture validation needs no private history. Some
capability evidence locators require private records to inspect their source bytes;
owner resolution, live archive readiness and relay installer evidence have the
explicit private or sibling-project dependencies documented above.
